server.name: ClickHouse MCP Cloud Server
server.title: ClickHouse Cloud MCP Server
server.description: Remote MCP server for ClickHouse Cloud. Lets agents discover your ClickHouse Cloud organizations and services, list databases and tables, inspect schemas, run SELECT queries, and look up ClickPipes, backups, and cost. Clients authenticate per user via OAuth, or for headless use with a ClickHouse Cloud API key sent as an HTTP Basic Authorization header (key ID as username, secret as password). Tool calls run with that user's or key's permissions, and a few tools are offered for only one credential type.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Read-only access to ClickHouse Cloud. Every tool runs as the authenticated user or API key, so results only include the organizations, services, and data that identity can see.

Start with get_organizations, then get_services_list with the organizationId to find service IDs and types. Use get_service_details for one service.

For ClickHouse services: call list_databases, then list_tables with the database name, then run_select_query with the serviceId. Only SELECT statements are accepted. Add LIMIT clauses and raise timeoutSeconds for long-running queries.

For Managed Postgres services: use run_postgres_select_query for read-only SQL, list_postgres_slow_query_patterns then get_postgres_slow_query_pattern_details to investigate slow queries, and get_postgres_metrics for time-series metrics.

Other tools cover ClickPipes, backups, organization cost, and service signals. Tools that need a specific authentication type or organization feature are omitted from the tool list when unavailable.

Idle services may be woken automatically; if a tool reports the service is not awake, retry after a short wait. If a query reports the user lacks passwordless access, the user must be granted access to that service in ClickHouse Cloud first.

tool.description: Returns the full definition of one ClickPipe on a ClickHouse service: name, description, state, replica scaling, source settings (Kafka, object storage, Kinesis, or Postgres), destination database and table definition, field mappings, and creation and update times. tool.name: list_postgres_slow_query_patterns
tool.title: List Postgres slow query patterns
tool.description: Lists the slowest query patterns observed on a Postgres service in a time window, with aggregate metrics per pattern (call count, total/avg/p50/p95/p99/max duration, rows, shared buffer cache hits and reads, CPU time, WAL bytes, error count). Durations are in microseconds. Use this first to find which queries dominate execution time, CPU, I/O, or WAL, then pass a selected pattern queryId, dbName, dbUser, dbOperation, and app exactly as returned to get_postgres_slow_query_pattern_details for its recent executions. Pass app as an empty string when the selected pattern has no application_name; omit the app filter only when intentionally querying across all applications. The queryText is normalized with $1-style placeholders.

app.description: Filter to a Postgres application_name. Pass an empty string to filter to queries with no application_name; omit to include all applications.

limit.description: Number of patterns per page. Omit for the default page of 20; use offset and the totalCount in the result to page further.

dbName.description: Only include patterns that ran in this database, matching the dbName of returned patterns.

dbUser.description: Only include patterns executed by this database user, matching the dbUser of returned patterns.

offset.description: Number of patterns to skip before the first returned pattern. Omit to start from the top-ranked pattern.

sortBy.description: Aggregate metric that ranks the patterns. Omit to rank by total_duration, which surfaces the patterns that consume the most execution time.

toDate.description: Inclusive end of the time window, evaluated at minute granularity. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-09T00:00:00.000Z.

fromDate.description: Inclusive start of the time window. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction. Omit for descending, which puts the heaviest patterns first.

dbOperation.description: Only include patterns with this top-level SQL operation type, such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or UTILITY, matching the dbOperation of returned patterns.

tool.name: get_postgres_slow_query_pattern_details
tool.title: Get Postgres slow query pattern details
tool.description: Returns up to the 10 most recent individual executions for a single Postgres slow query pattern from the last 24 hours, plus aggregate metrics for the pattern when available. For exact drill-down from list_postgres_slow_query_patterns, pass queryId, dbName, dbUser, dbOperation, and app exactly as returned; pass app as an empty string when the selected pattern has no application_name. Omit app only when intentionally querying across all applications. Each execution includes duration, rows, buffer/temp/WAL/JIT/CPU counters, and the error message and SQLSTATE if it failed. Durations are in microseconds. The execution sample is capped at 10 rows, so when aggregate is present rely on its fields for totals.

tool.title: Get Postgres metrics
tool.description: Returns bucketed time-series metrics for a Postgres service over a time window (CPU, memory, disk, network, connections, cache hit ratio, throughput, transactions, wait events, lock waits, and more). Wait metrics are active_sessions_by_wait (one series per wait event, such as Lock:relation, or None when a session is not waiting), lock_wait_time (p50, p95, and Max series, in seconds), and blocked_sessions. Each metric has a key, name, unit, description, and one series per label dimension, where each series is a list of (timestamp, value) data points. Timestamps are Unix seconds at the bucket start. Provide fromDate and toDate to bound the window; omit bucketSizeSeconds to let the server pick a bucket granularity for the window. Use this to chart or analyze how a service behaved over time.

toDate.description: Exclusive end of the time window. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-09T00:00:00.000Z.

fromDate.description: Inclusive start of the time window. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z.

serviceId.description: Managed Postgres service to read metrics for. Use the id of a postgres-type service returned by get_services_list.

organizationId.description: Organization that owns the Postgres service. Use the id of an organization returned by get_organizations.

bucketSizeSeconds.description: Width of each time bucket in seconds. Omit to let the server pick a granularity that suits the window; larger buckets return fewer data points.

message.description: Error message describing what went wrong

key.description: Stable metric identifier (e.g. cpu_usage, connection_count, cache_hit_ratio, active_sessions_by_wait)

unit.description: Unit of the metric values (e.g. %, IOPS, bytes/s, count)

label.description: Distinguishing label for this series within the metric (e.g. a CPU mode, a database name, a wait event such as "Lock:relation", or "Reads")

timestamp.description: Bucket start time as a Unix timestamp in seconds

dataPoints.description: Time-ordered data points, one per bucket

series.description: One series per label dimension of the metric

description.description: Human-readable description of what the metric measures

metrics.description: Available metrics, each with its bucketed time series

tool.name: list_databases
tool.title: List Databases
tool.description: Lists the databases in a ClickHouse Cloud service by running SHOW DATABASES as the authenticated identity. Returns only database names as an array of strings, with no tables, sizes, or other metadata; call list_tables with one of these names to see its tables and columns. If the query fails or the user lacks passwordless access to the service, result is an error object instead. Idle services are woken automatically and the call returns an error asking you to retry shortly; stopped services are never started automatically and must be started manually.

tool.name: list_tables
tool.title: List Tables
tool.description: Lists the tables of one database on a ClickHouse service by querying system.tables and system.columns as the authenticated identity, optionally narrowed with the like and notLike name patterns. Each table includes its engine and full engine definition, CREATE TABLE statement, sorting and primary keys, view dependencies, row, byte, part, and mark counts, comment, and its columns with type, default kind and expression, and comment. Returns an empty array when nothing matches. If the query fails or the user lacks passwordless access to the service, result is an error object instead. Idle services are woken automatically and the call returns an error asking you to retry shortly; stopped services are never started automatically and must be started manually.

tool.name: get_organization_cost
tool.title: Get Organization Cost
tool.description: Returns usage costs for an organization over an inclusive range of UTC calendar days from from_date to to_date (both required, at most 31 days). result has grandTotalCHC, the total in ClickHouse Credits (CHC), and costs, one record per day per billed entity (data warehouse, service, or ClickPipe) with the entity id and name, a per-metric CHC breakdown, the day total, and whether the record is final. On failure result is an error object with status "error" and a message.

to_date.description: Last day of the report, inclusive, as a UTC calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, e.g. 2024-12-20. The billing API requires it, and it can be at most 30 days after from_date, so one report covers at most 31 days.

from_date.description: First day of the report, inclusive, as a UTC calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, e.g. 2024-12-19. The billing API requires it: if omitted, the call returns an error result instead of defaulting to a period. Dates before 2022-10-01 are rejected.

organizationId.description: Organization to report costs for. Use the id of an organization returned by get_organizations.

costs.description: One record per day per billed entity, sorted by date, then entity type, then organization tier, then entity id. Each record has date (ISO-8601 day, UTC), entityType (datawarehouse, service, or clickpipe), entityId, entityName, dataWarehouseId, serviceId (null for datawarehouse entities), organizationTier (BASIC, SCALE, or ENTERPRISE, otherwise null), metrics (CHC per metric: storageCHC and backupCHC for data warehouses; computeCHC and data transfer metrics for services; computeCHC, dataTransferCHC, and initialLoadCHC for ClickPipes), totalCHC for the day, locked (true once the record is final), and an optional discount rate as a decimal fraction.

grandTotalCHC.description: Total cost across all returned records, in ClickHouse Credits (CHC)

_published_faq.name: How do I add ClickHouse Cloud MCP Server to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add ClickHouse Cloud MCP Server to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.clickhouse-dev.com/mcp.
